mechanics.name: Up the Ante
mechanics.currentEffect: Unlocks Self-Unhook attempts during the first Hook Stage for all Survivors. For every Survivor still in the Trial, gain 1 Token; each Token increases all Survivors' chance of succeeding at a Self-Unhook attempt by 1/2/3%, up to 3/6/9%.
activation: Survivors must attempt a Self-Unhook during the first Hook Stage to use the added Luck.
Ends/deactivates when: The token count and Luck bonus fall as Survivors leave the Trial.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (unknown): No material live balance change could be verified from available patch history.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Lets everyone attempt a first-stage self-unhook and improves the whole team's success chance while more Survivors remain.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Gain 1 token for each Survivor still in the Trial, up to the perk's maximum 3 tokens. Each token gives all Survivors 1/2/3% more Self-Unhook success chance, for a maximum 3/6/9%.
specialInteractions: The Luck bonus applies to every Survivor, not only the perk user.

editorial.summary: Grant teamwide Luck based on how many other Survivors remain alive, primarily affecting self-unhook chance; its old Slippery Meat combo no longer exists.
useCases: Give every Survivor access to first-stage self-unhook attempts without needing Deliverance.
Use in a coordinated team that wants to split pressure and reduce rescue obligations.
counters: Luck has almost no meaningful purpose outside self-unhook chance.
One copy alone still leaves self-unhooks unreliable compared with deterministic rescue perks.
The perk loses Luck as Survivors die, exactly when the team is already under pressure.
pros: Teamwide effect from one perk slot.
Unlocks a mechanic Survivors normally cannot rely on.
Scales brutally when multiple copies and Luck offerings are coordinated.
cons: Weak as a casual standalone perk.
RNG can fail at the worst moment.
Full ceiling demands heavy SWF coordination and multiple loadout commitments.
analysis: Up the Ante itself did not receive a 10.2 rework, but its practical ranking changed because Slippery Meat did. The old six-attempt Luck package that made coordinated self-unhook teams notorious is gone.
Teamwide Luck can still improve self-unhook odds and can still stack across a coordinated team, but it now has far less leverage without Slippery Meat multiplying the number of attempts.
That leaves an unusually narrow perk whose main outcome is still random. A safe normal rescue remains preferable whenever one is available.
The previous upper-B placement was built on an interaction that no longer exists and should be treated as invalid. Up the Ante now belongs in the independent reviewer’s lower-tier audit.
editorial.verdict: Collateral damage from the Slippery Meat rework. Up the Ante still boosts team Luck, but the coordinated self-unhook package lost the perk that made the odds explode.

archetypeRatings.note: Multiple copies plus Luck offerings can raise self-unhook odds, but the old Slippery Meat attempt-multiplication package is gone.
